steps.stem: When a new device replaces an older one, it is often called at first by the name of the device that it replaced, together with the element that it lacks: the radio, for example, was called at first "the wireless telegraph." In contrast, devices that are meant to replace an organ of the body, such as an artificial heart or an artificial limb, are named after the organ itself, since the organ remains the model by which they are judged. Which of the following could replace the example of the radio in the paragraph?
choices: The first cars were called "carriages without horses"
The first computers were called "electronic brains"
The first airplanes were called "flying machines"
The first television sets were called "radio with pictures"
explanation: Like the wireless telegraph, the car was named after the vehicle it replaced, together with the element that it lacks (the horses). (2) names a machine after an organ, which is the other kind of naming in the paragraph; (3) is not named after an earlier device; (4) names the new device after the old one together with an element that it adds, not one that it lacks.

steps.stem: A certain factory decided to give a bonus at the end of every month to each worker who had not been late to work even once during that month. The management found that since the bonus had been introduced, the total number of latenesses had indeed gone down, but that a worker who had been late once at the beginning of a month tended to be late many more times during the rest of that month. Which of the following cases is most similar to the case described?
choices: A bakery raised the price of its bread, and nevertheless it went on selling as many loaves as before
A newspaper stopped printing its weekly supplement, and after another newspaper began to print a similar supplement at no extra cost, many of its readers moved to the other newspaper
A library promised a free subscription to readers who returned all their books on time during a year. Readers who had once returned a book late no longer bothered to return their books on time
A company gave its workers an extra day off every month, and the output of the company grew
explanation: As in the factory, a reward is given only to those who never slip, so once someone has slipped he has nothing more to lose, and he stops trying. (1) is a price rise that did not cut demand, (2) is readers switching to another product, and (4) is a benefit that paid off.

steps.stem: Hila: "I have noticed that whenever Nadav's grades go down, his private teacher has already stopped coming to him. It seems that she loses her patience with him when he stops making an effort, and therefore she gives up on him every time his grades go down." Keren: "Your reasoning reminds me of the farmer who was sure that the crows bring the rain, since they always gather on his roof before a storm." What does Keren mean?
choices: Had Nadav's teacher gone on coming, his grades would have gone down even more
Nadav lets his grades go down because he wants his teacher to stop coming
Nadav's grades go down because his teacher stops coming to him
Nadav's teacher is wrong to give up on him exactly when he needs her most
explanation: The crows gather because a storm is coming, not the other way round: Keren says that Hila has reversed cause and effect. (1) adds a "what if", (2) adds a motive, and (4) adds a moral judgment.

steps.stem: Amnon, in a loud voice that was heard throughout the office: "Tzipi, I was told that you shouted at the new clerk this morning! Shouting at people does not help at all." Tzipi: "What you are doing now is like ____." Which of the following best completes Tzipi's words?
choices: refusing to lend a ladder to a neighbor because he once refused to lend you his
a speaker who lectures for two hours on the advantages of short speeches
watering the garden during the rain so that the plants will not dry out
blaming the thief because you left the door of the car open
explanation: Amnon shouts in order to say that shouting does not help, so his act undermines his own message, like a long lecture in praise of short speeches. (1) is retaliation, (3) is a pointless act, and (4) shifts the blame for one's own carelessness.

steps.stem: In a conversation between Orna and Eldad, Orna said something, and Eldad answered her: "You are like someone who decides whether a watermelon is sweet according to the sticker of the shop on it." Which of the following is most likely to be what Orna said?
choices: "I tried several pairs of shoes, and in the end I bought the most comfortable pair, even though it was the most expensive."
"The actors in the new play were so bad that I left in the middle."
"The coffee in the cafeteria is too bitter for me, and I will not drink it there again."
"Attorney Amir is certainly an excellent lawyer - his office is in the most expensive building in the city."
explanation: Eldad says that Orna judges the main thing by an incidental sign, as in judging a lawyer by his office building. (1), (2) and (3) each judge the thing itself: comfort, acting, taste.

steps.stem: Hagai told Boaz that he had ordered a rare cookbook from abroad and that it would arrive only in two months. Boaz answered him: "You are crossing the river by swimming, when the bridge is a few steps from you. In the city library there is a copy of the same book, and it has been standing on the shelf for years." In his answer, Boaz compares -
choices: the copy in the city library to the bridge
ordering the book from abroad to the river
the cookbook to the bridge
the copy ordered from abroad to swimming across the river
explanation: The bridge is the easy way to the same place: the library copy. Ordering from overseas is the swimming, not the river (2); the book is what lies on the other side, not the bridge (3); the ordered copy is the goal, not the effort of getting there (4).

steps.title: Parables and comparisons: what they ask
steps.intro: Name the question type, then work the way that type needs.

head: Question type
Typical wording
How to work
rows: Which example could replace… · explain in a similar way
Take the exact logic of the example; keep two, then compare precisely
Break the case into parts; match part by part
What does X mean? · What does X think?
Understand the parable, then translate it back to the conversation
Understand twice: the words, and every parable in the choices
What did X say / what was the context?
A parable answers something said, done or planned
In their reply, X compares ___ to -
Map each element of the parable to the real case

tips: Chicken and egg: check whether someone swapped cause and effect.
A parable is often a polite way of saying "that was a bit silly".
A true or sensible-sounding choice is not enough: it has to work the same way.

steps.stem: Over the past decade, Arnon Books, the largest publishing house in the country, has signed contracts with nearly every young poet whose work has appeared in the literary journals, although it publishes only a handful of their collections each year. The small presses, which once discovered most of the country's new poets, now publish almost no new poetry. In which of the following cases is the practice most similar to that of Arnon Books?
choices: A bakery chain buys the old bakery in each neighborhood it enters, keeps it open under the chain's name, and gradually replaces its products with the chain's own
A shoe manufacturer buys all its soles from a smaller competitor, so that the competitor comes to depend on its orders and can no longer afford to compete with it on price
A furniture maker buys large quantities of timber in the summer, when prices are low, and stores it until winter, when it uses the timber in its own workshops
A winery buys the entire harvest of the region's best vineyard, although it can use only part of the grapes, leaving the other wineries to make do with inferior fruit
explanation: Arnon Books takes more than it needs so that its competitors will not have it; the winery does the same with the grapes. (1) uses what it buys, (2) makes a competitor dependent, and (3) stores a resource for its own later use.

steps.stem: Professor Lahav found that students who attend the optional review sessions before the final exam in his course get higher grades than those who do not, and he is considering making the sessions compulsory. His teaching assistant remarked: "That is like concluding that umbrellas cause rain." Which of the following best expresses what the assistant meant?
choices: Compulsory sessions will not raise the grades of students who do not also prepare for the exam on their own
Students who are required to attend will pay less attention than those who come by choice, and so will gain less from the sessions
The students who are already doing well are the ones who choose to attend the review sessions
The sessions help only because Professor Lahav hints in them at what will appear on the exam
explanation: People carry umbrellas because rain is expected; umbrellas do not cause it. Likewise, students who are already doing well choose to attend, and the sessions are not the cause of their success. (1), (2) and (4) all accept that the sessions have some effect.

steps.stem: Dina, a first-year architecture student, described her first assignment to her father. He said: "That sounds like choosing curtains for a house that has not been built yet." Which of the following is most likely to have been Dina's assignment?
choices: To select colors and materials for the interior of a public building, although the building's plan will be drawn only at the end of the course
To visit three public buildings in the city and write a short description of each, before the buildings are discussed in class
To put together a portfolio of the sketches she made before starting her studies, so that the lecturer can assess her starting level
To write a short essay on the kind of buildings she hopes to design one day, although she has not yet taken any courses in design
explanation: Choosing curtains before the house exists is finishing something before its structure is there; selecting interior colors before the plan is drawn is the same. The other tasks do not depend on a stage that has not yet been done.

steps.stem: A printer bought an expensive press rather than a model that costs half as much and does the same work, explaining that ink for the cheaper model is so expensive that within two years it would cost him more than the difference in price. In which of the following cases is the reasoning most similar to the printer's?
choices: A runner trains on steep hills rather than on flat roads, accepting a harder training season in exchange for faster times in the races at the end of it
A couple chose to hold their wedding in the spring, when the hall they wanted charges less and the guests would not suffer from the heat
A commuter paid for an annual train pass, although it is expensive, because buying a ticket for each trip would cost him more over the year
A hiker paid more for a light tent than for the heavy one he already owned, so that he could cover more ground each day of his trek
explanation: The printer pays more once to avoid repeated costs that would add up to more; so does the commuter. (1) trades effort, not money, (2) chooses the cheaper option, and (4) pays more for a different kind of benefit.

steps.stem: After burglars took all of Galit's jewelry, her son urged her to install a safe. Galit replied: "Now? That is like calling the fire department after the house has burned down." Which of the following best expresses what Galit meant?
choices: A good safe would cost more than the few pieces of jewelry she still has
Her jewelry had been kept in a locked drawer, and the burglary showed that locks do not stop determined burglars
Burglars who managed to break into her apartment would have opened a safe as well, so a safe would not have helped even before the burglary
Installing a safe would have made sense before the burglary, but now there is nothing left for it to protect
explanation: Calling the fire department after the fire is acting when there is nothing left to save. (1) assumes some jewelry is left, (2) adds a fact that is not given, and (3) claims that a safe would never have helped.

steps.stem: The historian Malkiel describes two neighboring villages in the eighteenth century. When a flood destroyed the crops of the lower village, the upper village refused to share its grain. Two years later a drought struck the upper village, and the only help it received came from the lower village, which sent it seed for the following season. Which of the following cannot be learned from Malkiel's account?
choices: A community that refuses to help its neighbors may later find itself in need of their help
Help sometimes comes from the very people who were once refused it
A community that refused to help another has no right to accept help from it later
Being refused help does not necessarily make a community unwilling to help others
explanation: The upper village accepted the lower village's help, and nothing in the account suggests that it was wrong to do so. (1), (2) and (4) can all be learned from the account.

steps.stem: Eldad complained to Yaara that his neighbor talks too loudly in the stairwell. Yaara answered with the Talmudic saying: "When one says, 'Remove the splinter from between your teeth,' he is told, 'Remove the beam from between your eyes.'" Yaara was comparing -
choices: the neighbor's loud talking to the beam
Eldad to the splinter
the other tenants to the beam
Eldad's own faults to the beam
explanation: The one who points out another's splinter is told to remove the beam from his own eyes; Eldad, who complains about his neighbor, has greater faults of his own. The neighbor's loud talking corresponds to the splinter, not to the beam.

steps.stem: The larvae of certain beetles give off a scent resembling that of ant larvae. Worker ants carry them into the nest and feed them along with their own brood, and once grown, the beetle larvae feed on the ants' eggs. Which of the following is most similar to the behavior of the beetle larvae?
choices: A man joined a gang of thieves by passing himself off as a thief, and once the gang trusted him, he handed its members over to the police
A man passed himself off as a doctor in order to win his neighbors' admiration, but never treated anyone
A thief cut through the fence of a warehouse at night and stole the goods that were stored there
A new employee who was hired on his cousin's recommendation, without any pretense, gradually persuaded the owner to dismiss the veteran workers
explanation: The larvae are accepted because they pass for members of the colony and then harm it from within; so does the man in the gang. In (2) the disguise harms no one, in (3) there is no acceptance, and in (4) there is no disguise.

steps.stem: Yoni's son was painting his room, and drops of paint were falling on the floor. When Yoni asked why he was not wiping them up, his son answered: "Nobody washes the dishes in the middle of cooking." In his answer, the son compares painting the room to -
choices: washing the dishes after the meal
cooking
the dirty dishes that pile up in the sink
wiping up the drops of paint
explanation: Cooking, like painting, is the work that makes the mess, and washing the dishes, like wiping up the drops, is left for the end. (1) and (4) are the cleaning, and (3) is the mess itself.

steps.stem: Some manufacturers of vegetable oil print on the bottle, in large letters, the words "contains no cholesterol." Cholesterol is found only in foods of animal origin, so no vegetable oil contains it. Nevertheless, such labels lead many consumers to prefer the bottles on which they appear to other bottles of oil. In which of the following cases is the consumers' behavior most similar to the behavior described?
choices: Many people prefer to buy a washing machine in a store that advertises free delivery, although all the stores in the city deliver free
After reading a report about mercury in fish, a man stopped buying fish, even the kinds that contain almost no mercury
A woman postponed a trip abroad after she heard news of an epidemic in a neighboring country, although the epidemic had not reached her destination
A man checks the brakes of every car he rents, although the rental company promises that its cars are checked before every rental
explanation: The consumers are drawn by an advantage that is true of every product of the kind; free delivery, offered by all the stores, is such an advantage. (2) and (3) are exaggerated reactions to a danger, and (4) is extra caution.

steps.stem: For a whole week, everyone in Kornblit's office talked about the bow tie he wore one day. Asked why a tie should cause such a stir, he said: "Our office is like a very quiet room: even the ticking of a clock sounds loud there." According to Kornblit -
choices: his colleagues enjoy gossiping about one another, and any change in a colleague's appearance gives them something to talk about for days
he is known for dressing in a way that attracts attention, and this time too his colleagues noticed what he was wearing
so little changes in his office that even a minor change stands out
a bow tie is so unusual that it would have attracted attention in any office
explanation: A ticking clock sounds loud only because the room is quiet; the tie was noticed only because so little changes in the office. (1) explains the talk by gossip, (2) contradicts the smallness of the change, and (4) attributes the attention to the tie itself.

steps.stem: Traffic engineers have noticed that on some mountain roads, fewer accidents occur on sharp bends that drivers regard as dangerous than on the straight sections of the same road. One explanation is that drivers who fear the bends slow down and drive more carefully as they approach them. In which of the following cases is the explanation most similar to the one described?
choices: Novice riders fall off horses more often than experienced riders, because they have not yet learned to keep their balance when the horse changes pace
Speakers who are afraid of forgetting their lines often do forget them, because their anxiety keeps them from concentrating on what they are saying
Fewer people fall on the riverside path at night since lamps were installed along it, because they can now see the stones on the path
Hikers get lost less often on unfamiliar trails than on familiar ones, because on an unfamiliar trail they consult the map more often
explanation: The danger people expect makes them more careful, and so there are fewer mishaps; the same is true of the hikers. In (1) lack of skill causes the falls, in (2) fear causes the mishap, and in (3) the danger itself was reduced.

steps.stem: At a literary conference, a novelist complained that critics had found in her latest book a political message she had never intended. One of the critics replied: "Once a letter has been sent, it is the recipient, not the sender, who decides how to read it." Which of the following can be inferred from the critic's reply?
choices: Once a book is published, its readers, not its author, determine its meaning
Critics are under no obligation to accept an author's explanation of her own book, and certainly not to praise the book on that basis
Even readers who know a book thoroughly cannot discover what its author intended, since authors rarely state their intentions explicitly
The novelist herself may come to read her book differently in a few years, when she is no longer as close to it as she is now
explanation: The sender does not control how a letter is read, and the author does not control what readers find in a published book. (2) concerns praise, (3) concerns discovering the intention, which the critic does not discuss, and (4) concerns the author's own reading.

steps.stem: Every buyer who came to see the Havkins' apartment offered less than the family was asking, and the family decided to advertise the apartment in a different newspaper. Their real estate agent said: "Putting a picture in a new frame does not change what people think of the picture." Which of the following best expresses what the agent meant?
choices: The buyers who have already seen the apartment are the only serious ones, and the family should accept the best of their offers
New buyers will react to the same asking price as the previous ones did, so it is the price that must change
Buyers who read the other newspaper tend to offer even less than those who read the first one
Instead of looking for new buyers, the family should try to persuade those who have already seen the apartment to raise their offers
explanation: A new frame leaves the picture unchanged, and a new newspaper leaves the offer unchanged; new buyers will judge the same price in the same way. (1) and (4) concern the earlier buyers, and (3) predicts lower offers, which does not follow.

steps.stem: At a board meeting of a chamber orchestra, it was proposed that the orchestra reduce its deficit by dismissing its two soloists, who receive the highest salaries. One board member objected that this would be "sawing off the branch we are sitting on." Which of the following is most likely to be what he meant?
choices: The soloists' salaries account for only a small part of the orchestra's expenses, so dismissing them would hardly reduce the deficit
Most of the audience comes to hear the soloists, so without them the orchestra's income would fall
Rather than dismissing musicians, the orchestra should hire more of them, so that it can perform larger and more popular works
Other orchestras would be quick to hire the soloists, and the orchestra would be unable to bring them back when its finances improve
explanation: The branch is what holds the orchestra up: the soloists bring in its income. (1) says only that the saving is small, and (3) and (4) do not concern the source of income.

steps.stem: Nurit: "Should it be proven beyond doubt that Pomerantz wrote the manuscript, I would still deny it, because I am certain that he did not write it." Which of the following contradictions is most similar to the contradiction in Nurit's words?
choices: "It has indeed been shown that the comet will pass close to the earth, but I cannot tell whether it will pass close, since this has not yet been shown"
"Even if it turns out that most critics admire the film, I will go on watching it, since I do not enjoy it"
"Many restaurants are indeed overpriced, but some must be reasonably priced, since I have eaten at few overpriced ones"
"Even if it is shown that most cyclists are thin, I will not accept that many cyclists are heavy, since most thin people are cyclists"
explanation: Nurit grants a proof and then denies its conclusion on the strength of the very claim the proof refutes; (1) has the same shape (shown / not shown). (2) is not a contradiction, and (3) and (4) are faulty inferences of other kinds.

steps.stem: Some argue that in order to understand a person's character we should examine his recent experiences and not his early childhood. A psychologist disagreed and illustrated her position with an analogy: "What would we think of a gardener who, noting that the lamp on his porch is far closer to his plants than the sun, concluded that the lamp does much more to make them grow than the sun does?" In saying this, the psychologist compares -
choices: early childhood to the plants
recent experiences to the porch lamp
early childhood to the porch lamp
recent experiences to the sun
explanation: The lamp is near but has little influence, like recent experiences; the sun is far but decisive, like early childhood. (3) and (4) swap the two, and (1) makes childhood the thing influenced.

steps.stem: Galia: "The proportion of residents over 80 in our town is the highest in the country, so something about life here must lengthen people's lives." Na'or: "You might just as well say that hospitals make people ill, since that is where most sick people are found." Which of the following is most likely to be the point on which Na'or's reply is based?
choices: Many elderly people move to the town from elsewhere, drawn by its services for the elderly
The town's air is exceptionally clean, and clean air is known to lengthen life
Few children are born in the town, so the elderly make up a larger share of its population than they otherwise would
The town is so small that a handful of long-lived residents is enough to raise the proportion considerably
explanation: Sick people come to hospitals; hospitals do not make them sick. Likewise, elderly people come to the town, and the town does not make them live long. (2) supports Galia, and (3) and (4) point to errors that the comparison does not express.

steps.stem: Asaf has been taking guitar lessons for three weeks. Every few days he tries to play a whole song from beginning to end, and each time he fails, he considers giving up. His teacher told him: "If you keep opening the oven to see whether the cake has risen, it never will." In her reply, the teacher was comparing -
choices: Asaf's thoughts of giving up to the oven
the songs Asaf wants to learn to the oven
Asaf's thoughts of giving up the lessons to opening the oven
Asaf's attempts to play a whole song to opening the oven
explanation: Opening the oven is checking too early whether the cake has risen; this is what Asaf does each time he tries to play a whole song after only a few weeks. His thoughts of giving up are the result of these checks, not the checks themselves, and the oven does not correspond to the songs.

steps.stem: In a conversation with Ronen, Adi said: "That is always the way: the day you bring a ladder, the cat climbs down from the tree by itself." Which of the following could Ronen have said to prompt Adi's remark?
choices: "I studied for the exam for two months, and on the morning of the exam I came down with a fever and could not take it."
"This time I took a spare tire on the trip, and of course none of the tires went flat."
"My car, which had not given me any trouble for three years, broke down on the morning of my job interview."
"I baked my neighbor a birthday cake, only to find out that she does not eat sweets at all."
explanation: Adi means that the one time a person prepares for a problem, the problem does not occur. Only in (2) was a precaution taken that turned out to be unnecessary; (1), (3) and (4) describe plain bad luck.

steps.stem: Bella said: "Car thieves in our city steal mainly new cars, and so my car, which is twelve years old, will not be stolen." Which of the following arguments is most similar to Bella's argument?
choices: Swimming in the sea is not dangerous when there is a lifeguard on the beach, so if I swim only when he is there, nothing will happen to me
Mosquitoes are attracted mainly to people who sweat, and since I sweat a great deal in the summer, I will be bitten more than my brother
The Tamuz Company hires mainly candidates who have a university degree, and so I, who have no degree, will not be hired there
The flowers in the garden make me sneeze, so if I am not sneezing today, it means that the flowers in the garden have not yet opened
explanation: Bella turns "mainly new cars" into "never an old car"; (3) turns "mainly candidates with a degree" into "never a candidate without one". (1) does not start from a preference, (2) concludes that the preferred group will be affected more, which does follow, and (4) reasons back from an effect that did not occur.

steps.stem: The philosopher Gavish poses the following problem: twenty trees are not a forest, but a thousand trees are, and adding a single tree to a group of trees that is not a forest does not turn it into one. It therefore seems impossible to say at which tree a group of trees becomes a forest. In which of the following cases is the difficulty most similar to the one Gavish describes?
choices: A runner's time is recorded only at the finish line, so while the race is under way it cannot be known whether he is on his way to breaking the record
Everyone agrees that a person of twenty is young and a person of eighty is not, yet no one can name the birthday on which a person stops being young
Since people differ in how much noise they can tolerate, there is no volume at which everyone at a party would agree that the music is too loud
How tall a young tree will grow over the next twenty years depends on how much rain falls in those years, which no one can predict
explanation: Small steps lead from one clear state to its opposite without any single step at which the change occurs; the same is true of youth and age. (1) and (4) concern knowledge of the future, and (3) concerns differences between people.

steps.stem: Historians of science have described the following phenomenon: a scientist who is already well known receives more credit for a discovery than an unknown scientist who made a similar discovery, so that the gap between them keeps widening. Which of the following is the best example of a similar phenomenon in another field?
choices: A singer whose first record was a success is invited onto more radio programs than other singers, and as a result his next record also outsells theirs
A student who failed his first exam began studying with a private tutor, and by the end of the year he had the highest grades in his class
A company that cut its prices attracted many new customers, but because of the lower prices its profits at the end of the year did not rise
A painter whose work was ignored in his lifetime became famous after his death, and his paintings now sell for very high prices
explanation: An existing advantage brings further advantages, and the gap grows; only the singer's first success brings him more exposure and more success. (2) is improvement after failure, (3) has no advantage that grows, and (4) is late recognition.

steps.stem: For years Doron has tried to save money, without success. He told a friend: "This time I am going to do what my grandfather did when his doctor forbade him to eat sugar - he gave the key to the sugar cupboard to his neighbor." Which of the following is most likely to be Doron's plan?
choices: Each time he breaks the promise he made himself to save, he will give a sum to charity, and each time the sum will be larger than the time before
He will read about people who reached old age without any savings, so that the fear of ending up like them will keep him from spending
He will have his bank transfer part of his salary each month to a savings account from which no money can be withdrawn for five years
He will set himself a strict monthly budget and keep a record of every purchase he makes
explanation: The grandfather did not rely on his own willpower but gave up his access to the sugar in advance; Doron does the same when he arranges that the money cannot be withdrawn. (1), (2) and (4) all still depend on his own willpower.

steps.stem: The staff of a small company must submit a grant application in French within a week. Yaron proposed that they translate it themselves: "If we pay a translator every time, we will never learn French ourselves." Hadas replied: "You do not learn to swim when the boat is already sinking." Which of the following cannot be inferred from the conversation?
choices: Yaron believes that paying a translator would solve the company's problem only for this application
Hadas believes that there is not enough time now for the staff to translate the application themselves
Both Yaron and Hadas regard knowledge of French as a skill that the staff would have to acquire through their own effort
Hadas disagrees with Yaron that, in general, it is better for the staff to know French than to depend on a translator
explanation: Hadas objects only to learning at the last moment, not to learning; nothing she says rejects the view that knowing French is better. (1), (2) and (3) can be inferred.

steps.stem: A mayor decided to stop publishing the annual survey in which residents rate the city's services. A member of the city council told him: "You are like a sick man who covers the mirror so as not to see how pale he is." It follows that, in the council member's view -
choices: preparing the survey takes up too much of the municipal staff's time, which could be put to better use
the city can no longer afford the survey, and the mayor is using the budget cuts as an excuse to drop it
the last survey showed that residents are dissatisfied with the city's services
publishing the survey every year prompts residents to flood the municipality with complaints
explanation: Covering the mirror hides the illness without curing it; the council member means that the survey showed something bad that the mayor prefers not to see. (1) and (2) are practical reasons, and in (4) the problem is the complaints, not what the survey shows.

steps.stem: People say of Hofman, who manages the most successful branch of a large bank, that the wind is always at his back. Which of the following is not implied by this remark?
choices: The branch owes its success mainly to its experienced and skilled staff rather than to Hofman's management
The branch is located in the city's wealthiest neighborhood and would succeed under almost any manager
Customers are drawn by the bank's good reputation, from which Hofman's branch benefits more than others
Hofman has succeeded because of his skill in managing the branch under difficult conditions
explanation: A wind at one's back is a force that is not one's own and makes the going easy; (1), (2) and (3) each name such a force. (4) attributes the success to Hofman's own skill under difficult conditions, the opposite of the remark.
